title: Power Brake System: Diagnostic Starting Point
introduction:
The brake booster reduces the driver effort needed to operate the brakes. The master cylinder develops hydraulic pressure, and the calipers turn that pressure into pad force against the discs. I think of the booster as a helping hand for your foot; keeping its role distinct from pressure generation makes the system easier to understand.

Start by describing the pedal feel and the conditions under which the concern appears. A pedal concern and a friction-material concern can require different tests, so the symptom is the opening clue, not a booster diagnosis. Continue with the required brake-system diagnostic referral below. This page contains no booster test setup, measurements or result branches and is not a standalone diagnostic procedure.

edits.text: For power brake system diagnosis, refer to Brake System (206-00 Brake System - General Information, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: Understanding the booster's assistance role helps frame the complaint, but it cannot establish a fault. The shared diagnostic procedure supplies the path needed to evaluate the concern.
